script.speaker: narrator
script.line: High above the sleepy town lived a tiny, nervous star named Starlight.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: One night, Starlight felt very dim.

script.speaker: char1
script.line: Oh dear, I don't think my light is bright enough tonight. Maybe I should just hide.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: The big, wise Moon was watching nearby.

script.speaker: char2
script.line: Starlight, why are you frowning? You look wonderful!

script.speaker: char1
script.line: But look! That star is huge and sparkly! My light is just a tiny flicker.

script.speaker: char2
script.line: A tiny flicker is exactly what someone needs. Every light, no matter how small, guides a sailor home or helps a firefly find a flower.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Starlight thought about this. He decided to try his best.

script.speaker: char1
script.line: You’re right, Moon! I will shine as brightly as I can, just for me.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Starlight puffed up his chest and shone! His tiny, cheerful light joined the sky, making the night perfect.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: The end.

title: Freddy the Frog and the Fast River

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Freddy the Frog loved his little pond, but he dreamed of the big, wide river.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: One morning, Freddy decided to jump in!

script.speaker: char1
script.line: Whee! This current is so fast! I'm moving! I'm going to see the whole world!

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Suddenly, a big log zipped past and knocked Freddy off balance. He felt scared.

script.speaker: char2
script.line: Woah there, little hopper! You look a bit green around the gills.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: It was Turtle, floating by on a mossy stone.

script.speaker: char1
script.line: I wanted to be fast, but this river is too fast! I can't keep up, and I don't know where I'm going.

script.speaker: char2
script.line: You don't always need to be fast. Sometimes you need to be strong and steady. Grab onto my shell and let's go slow. We'll find a nice quiet eddy.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Freddy held on tight to Turtle. They drifted slowly until they reached a calm, safe pool.

script.speaker: char1
script.line: Thank you, Turtle. Slow and steady really does win the day.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: The end.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Leo the Lion cub was coloring a sunset, but he couldn't find his favorite red crayon.

script.speaker: char1
script.line: Where is it? I can't color the sun without red! I'll never finish my picture!

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Pencil, who was resting nearby, rolled closer.

script.speaker: char2
script.line: Calm down, Leo. When you're angry, you can't see anything clearly. Let's look together.

script.speaker: char1
script.line: But I've looked everywhere! It’s gone forever! Everything is ruined!

script.speaker: char2
script.line: We need to use our detective eyes. What did you color last? Think hard.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Leo closed his eyes and remembered he had been drawing a giant, red apple.

script.speaker: char1
script.line: The apple! I put it away with the fruit basket drawing on the shelf!

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: Leo rushed to the shelf and found the red crayon tucked safely inside the basket drawing.

script.speaker: char2
script.line: See? Slow thinking is always better than fast worrying.

script.speaker: char1
script.line: You're right, Pencil. Thanks for helping me pause and think.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line: The end.
